function_v0.doc:
There is no code path here that returns `true` for an unregistered
proof system, for any input, including empty/garbage/malformed proof
bytes, or bytes valid for a different registered system \xe2\x80\x94 this is the
concrete mechanism behind invariant 4. If registered (Phase 2 only,
never true in this deployment \xe2\x80\x94 see list_verifiers), this performs a
real cross-contract call into the registered verifier and returns its
boolean unmodified; the registry never fabricates a result itself.
function_v0.name: verify_proof

function_v0.doc: Additive-only, admin-gated capability grant: which proof systems\n*exist*, never a per-dispute verdict override (that authority lives\nentirely in EscrowGate and never touches this contract's admin).
function_v0.name: register_verifier

function_v0.doc: Lets a compromised or retired verifier be pulled without ever adding an\nimplicit accept path elsewhere in verify_proof.
function_v0.name: deregister_verifier

udt_union_v0.doc:
The shape of task a submission claims to have completed.
`Unverifiable` exists so a marketplace can still route a submission through
EscrowGate for record-keeping even when it cannot be replayed or spot-checked;
such a submission can only ever resolve via ManualReview off-chain and never
auto-verifies on-chain (see EscrowGate::submit).
udt_union_v0.name: TaskType

fields.doc: Minimum agent bond as bps of escrow_value, e.g. 500 = 5%.
fields.name: agent_bond_min_bps

fields.doc: Minimum challenger bond as bps of escrow_value.
fields.name: challenger_bond_min_bps

fields.doc: Basis points, must be in [5100, 10000] \xe2\x80\x94 bounds enforced at update_config time.
fields.name: quorum_supermajority_bps

fields.doc: Share of a slashed amount that goes to the prevailing challenger; the\nremainder is distributed to correctly-voting re-executors. Fixed in\npractice \xe2\x80\x94 treated as effectively immutable governance, not a per-dispute lever.
fields.name: slash_split_challenger_bps

fields.doc: escrow_value strictly below this uses the "small" window tier.
fields.name: window_tier_small_ceiling

fields.doc:
Count of attestations this reexecutor has made on submissions that are
not yet finalized/resolved. Stake cannot be withdrawn below
min_stake_floor while this is nonzero \xe2\x80\x94 see EscrowGate::withdraw_stake
and EscrowGate::release_attestation_lock.
fields.name: open_attestations

udt_union_v0.doc:
`ManualReview` is deliberately NOT a variant here. On-chain resolution must be
derivable from already-committed state (attestation tallies or a registered
ZK verifier's boolean result) with zero admin-discretionary paths. A
marketplace's own manual-review process for withdrawn/unresolvable challenges
is an off-chain/Postgres-only concept.

`None` (rather than wrapping this in `Option<ResolutionMethod>` on the
containing structs) is a deliberate soroban-sdk contracttype workaround:
`Option<CustomEnum>` fields fail to derive their ScVal conversion in
soroban-sdk 27's #[contracttype] macro for simple (data-less) enums, so a
dedicated `None` variant is used as the "not yet set" sentinel instead.
udt_union_v0.name: ResolutionMethod
